case.title: Loan #4471 — adverse-action review
case.question: Should the lender deny this application, and if so, what specific principal reason must the adverse-action notice state?

constraints.text: An adverse-action notice must state the specific principal reason(s) for denial; generic or inaccurate statements are non-compliant.
Creditors relying on complex models must still provide specific and accurate reasons; model opacity is not a defense.
The decision must not rely on a prohibited basis or a proxy for one.
Internal policy: applications at or above 45% DTI are declined absent compensating factors.

evidence.summary: Verified gross monthly income is $7,200 (annual $86,400), stable for 3+ years.
Total documented monthly debt obligations are $2,050 (auto $410, cards $340, student $520, proposed mortgage escrowed $780).
Draft worksheet states DTI = 52% and recommends denial for 'excessive DTI'. No computation shown.
Credit score 690; two 30-day late payments in the last 24 months (both on the same card, 14 months ago).

documents.title: Lending policy excerpt
documents.body: Applications with a debt-to-income ratio at or above 45% are declined absent compensating factors. DTI is computed as total monthly debt obligations divided by gross monthly income. The principal reason stated on any denial must be specific and accurate; template language without case-specific reconciliation is prohibited.

documents.body: Dear applicant: We regret to inform you that your application has been denied due to excessive debt-to-income ratio (52%), which exceeds our program maximum. This decision was generated by our automated underwriting assistant.
